documents.title: Academic Integrity: Use of Artificial Intelligence
documents.summary: Academic Senate statement on AI inside De Anza's academic integrity page. It defers to course-specific instructor policies, falls back to the district student-conduct standards when none exists, and asks students to ensure submitted work reflects their own knowledge and to ask when unsure.
documents.stance_why: The policy sets no stance of its own: "If your instructor has established a course-specific policy on AI use, you are expected to follow those guidelines", with only a conduct-standards fallback, so decisions are delegated to instructors.

units.why: The preamble says AI tools "can enhance student learning and support academic success"; it frames the college's purpose for AI use, so it is an institution-level framework statement (P56) rather than a rule, hence informs/neutral.
units.anchor: can enhance student learning and support academic success
units.policy: De Anza College recognizes that AI tools have a range of applications that can enhance student learning and support academic success.

units.why: "AI can also be misused in ways that undermine the learning process" gives the reason for limits: misuse harms learning. It fits P41 (limits protect learning) better than P53, which covers ethical harms.
units.anchor: AI can also be misused in ways that undermine the learning process
units.policy: AI can be misused in ways that undermine the learning process.

units.why: "If your instructor has established a course-specific policy on AI use, you are expected to follow those guidelines" leaves the rule to each instructor and binds students; P04 (instructor sets the rule) fits, not P11, which is about non-carryover.
units.anchor: you are expected to follow those
units.policy: If an instructor has established a course-specific policy on AI use, students are expected to follow those guidelines.

units.why: "In the absence of a specific policy, students must use AI tools in accordance with the ... policy on Standards of Student Conduct" is the fallback when a course is silent, so P06.
units.anchor: In the absence of a specific policy, students must use AI tools in accordance
units.policy: In the absence of a specific policy, students must use AI tools in accordance with the Foothill-De Anza Community College District policy on Standards of Student Conduct.

units.why: "the work submitted represents the students' knowledge and skills" says submitted work must reflect the student's own ability, i.e. ownership of what is submitted (P29) rather than a ban on specific uses (P19).
units.anchor: the work submitted represents the students’ knowledge and skills
units.policy: When students use AI, the work submitted represents the students' knowledge and skills.

units.why: "If you are uncertain about appropriate AI use in your coursework, consult your instructor for clarification" tells unsure students to ask the instructor first: P10.
units.anchor: If you are uncertain about appropriate AI use in your coursework
units.policy: If you are uncertain about appropriate AI use in your coursework, consult your instructor for clarification.

units.why: "It is the responsibility of the faculty to clearly define the requirements and rules applicable to their courses" requires instructors to communicate rules (here covering AI use by reference); closest is P09, though it does not name the syllabus or AI.
units.frag_end: applicable to their courses for all students
units.policy: It is the responsibility of the faculty to clearly define the requirements and rules applicable to their courses for all students.

units.why: "work which in some way circumvents the given rules and regulations, will not be tolerated" holds the student to personal effort and the rules; general integrity text that governs AI use, so P29 (own work) is the nearest type.
units.anchor: work which in some way circumvents the given rules and regulations
units.policy: The submission of work that is not the product of a student's personal effort, or work which in some way circumvents the given rules and regulations, will not be tolerated.

notes: Single university-layer document; no school, computing or course policies found. Units 7 and 8 come from the general integrity text around the AI section and are not AI-specific.
